title: We built an open-source self-hosted alternative to [popular analytics] — here's how it works
body: After months of frustration with SaaS analytics that collect too much data, we shipped a zero-knowledge, self-hosted analytics stack. It runs on a single VPS, ships under 50MB, and respects user privacy by default. Happy to answer questions.

title: Why on-chain analytics doesn't have to mean surrendering your data to a third party
body: Most crypto analytics tools today still rely on centralized data lakes. We reversed the model: everything stays in your infra, queries stay local, and you get the same insight depth. Early feedback welcome.

title: Show: lightweight blockchain indexer with pluggable storage backends
body: Built a modular indexer that works with EVM chains and can store data in SQLite, Postgres, or flat files. It's extensible, has a clean API, and the core is under 2k LOC. Links in comments.

title: Open-source observability stack that actually runs on a Raspberry Pi
body: We optimized our entire stack for ARM and low-memory environments. Metrics, logs, and traces — all in one binary, no separate services needed. Here are the benchmarks and setup steps.

title: Self-hosted analytics, logging, and uptime monitoring in 3 Docker containers
body: Replaced Datadog and UptimeRobot with our own stack. Total cost: $0. Total containers: 3. Total setup time: 12 minutes. Full config included.

title: How we made wallet connect work offline with local-first auth
body: Offline-first auth for dApps is hard. We built a proof-of-concept that syncs when connectivity returns, no custodial bridge required. Open for contributors.

title: Tracking DeFi yields without relying on centralized APIs
body: Our tool reads chain state directly from RPC nodes and computes APY/APY without third-party data providers. Zero trust, zero leakage. Demo and repo inside.

title: Smart contract event indexing in under 100 lines of Rust
body: We extracted our event indexer from a larger project. It filters, parses, and stores contract events with minimal overhead. Feedback on API design appreciated.

title: We replaced our entire cloud logging pipeline with a single open-source binary
body: Loki + Promtail felt overkill. Our binary ships structured logs, tail-based sampling, and a tiny query engine. Here's the migration story.

title: Self-hosted CI/CD for personal projects that actually respects your hardware
body: GitHub Actions eats free tier limits. Our self-hosted runner manager reuses idle cycles, supports ARM, and gives you full pipeline visibility. Free and open source.

title: Thread: We rebuilt web3 analytics from scratch. Here are 7 mistakes we made so you don't have to.
body: 1/ We assumed everyone wanted dashboards. They wanted raw queries. 2/ We over-engineered auth. 3/ We ignored self-hosters. 4/ We shipped before benchmarks. 5/ We forgot offline use cases. 6/ We treated docs as an afterthought. 7/ We didn't listen to the first 10 users. Full thread on what we learned.

title: Single post: Just open-sourced our entire analytics stack. Zero telemetry, zero cloud lock-in, zero cost. Link in bio.
body: If you've ever wanted to own your data stack end-to-end, this is for you. Self-host in 5 minutes or run it on your laptop.

title: Thread: The case against vendor lock-in in crypto analytics, and what we built instead.
body: 1/ Vendor lock-in isn't just pricing — it's data gravity. 2/ Most 'on-chain' tools still stream your queries to AWS. 3/ Self-hosting used to be painful. 4/ We changed that with a single binary. 5/ Here's the architecture. 6/ Here's how to try it in 2 commands. 7/ Here's what's next.

title: Single post: Hot take — if your analytics tool can't run offline, it's not analytics, it's surveillance.
body: Unpopular opinion? Let's discuss.

title: Thread: How to go from zero to self-hosted observability in under 10 minutes.
body: 1/ Clone repo. 2/ docker compose up. 3/ Open port 3000. 4/ Done. In this thread, I'll share the exact config we use for metrics, logs, and uptime — plus how to back it up to S3 or local disk.

title: Thread: Why we chose Rust for our analytics engine — and why it matters for self-hosters.
body: 1/ Memory safety = fewer crashes on small boxes. 2/ Single binary = no runtime install. 3/ Async I/O = efficient under load. 4/ Tiny surface area = easier to audit. 5/ WASM target = run in browser. 6/ We compiled to ARM in 2 hours. 7/ Here's the memory profile.

title: Show HN: We built a self-hosted analytics stack that runs on a Raspberry Pi
body: After testing every open-source analytics tool available, we decided to build our own. It includes metrics, logs, and uptime monitoring in a single binary with zero external dependencies. Happy to answer questions about architecture, performance, or roadmap.

title: Ask HN: What's missing from current self-hosted observability tools?
body: We're building an open-source observability stack and want to hear from the HN community. What do you wish existed today that doesn't? What's broken in the current offerings? What would make you switch?

title: Show HN: Open-source blockchain indexer with pluggable storage (SQLite, Postgres, flat files)
body: Built a lightweight indexer for EVM chains that's storage-backend agnostic. Core is under 2k LOC, extensible via plugins, and designed for local-first workflows. Would love feedback from people running their own nodes.

title: Ask HN: Best practices for self-hosting with limited hardware?
body: We're seeing more users run our stack on Raspberry Pi and old laptops. What hardware constraints do you push against? How do you handle backups, updates, and monitoring on low-power machines?

title: Show HN: Zero-knowledge analytics – query your data without sending it anywhere
body: Our new query engine runs entirely client-side or on your own server. No telemetry, no cloud processing, no data leakage. Built for teams that need insight without exposure. Benchmark results and source inside.

title: Why we invested in privacy-first infrastructure instead of chasing AI hype
body: The market is flooded with AI wrappers. We chose a harder path: build reliable, open-source infrastructure that respects user data. Here's why privacy-first isn't just ethical — it's becoming a competitive advantage.

title: The case for local-first engineering in 2026
body: Remote work normalized async. Cloud centralization normalized surveillance. Local-first is the next logical step. As engineers, we should build tools that work offline, respect ownership, and don't phone home. Our new open-source release is a step in that direction.

title: We just open-sourced our entire analytics stack. Here's what the business case looks like.
body: Cost: $0. Lock-in: zero. Speed: 2x faster than our previous SaaS. Team size: 3 engineers. Sometimes the best infrastructure decision is to stop renting and start owning. Details inside.

title: Hiring: Remote engineers who believe open source is a competitive moat
body: We're a small, distributed team building privacy-first observability. We value craft over hype, depth over breadth, and shipping over meeting. If you want to work on real infrastructure, reach out.

title: How self-hosted tools changed our startup's runway by 40%
body: By replacing six SaaS subscriptions with self-hosted equivalents, we cut recurring costs, removed vendor risk, and gained full control over our data. Here's the exact stack and the math.
